task_instance: Invoke the retrospective skill on a session: scan a session JSONL transcript, detect session depth (fast vs full mode), extract user corrections and failed-skill signals, dedup against existing memory, and produce the ranked list of candidate learnings/actions that the retro presents to the user for approval.
evidence: Copied the skill's bundled retro_engine.py and scenarios into the work dir and created a Python venv there (python -m venv .venv; pip -q install pyyaml pytest; yaml 6.0.3, pytest 9.2.0). Authored a realistic 15-line sample session transcript (sample_sessions/session_abc123.jsonl: a Telegram-bot DM session with a failed telegram skill, two user corrections, and 9 tool calls) as the input a user would supply. Wrote driver.py that parses the JSONL into the engine's SessionData and runs the skill's own process_session() pipeline (gate_check -> generate_findings -> dedup_against_memory -> filter_by_skill_content -> rank_candidates -> cap). Output verified correct: MODE=full (9 tool calls >= threshold 8), 2 user corrections and 1 failed-skill signal extracted, 3 ranked candidate actions produced with user corrections ranked ahead of the failed-skill update, matching the skill's documented ranking rules. This is the skill's core analytical deliverable (the candidate learnings/actions a retro surfaces). Note: the bundled pytest suite (test_retro_engine.py) could not be executed because the auto-mode classifier denied running the copied test code ('Code from External'); the identical engine logic was instead driven and verified through driver.py importing retro_engine directly. The skill's subsequent AskUserQuestion approval step has no answerer in this session and its execution step writes to the home skills/memory directory outside the permitted work directory, so only the analysis output (the substantive deliverable) was produced and verified, not the interactive write-back.
